app.title: LAFF Viewer: browser for automated light-curve fit results
app.summary: A person picks a release of the fitted results and plots one parameter against another across the whole catalogue. They can switch between log and linear axes, colour the points by a third parameter or highlight chosen items, and show either or both of two component populations. Clicking a point, or typing a name, opens that item's page. The page shows its summary values, its fitted model figure from each instrument, and tables of every fitted component with derived energetics and model parameters. An about page defines each parameter and how it was computed.

task.text: Explore how fitted and derived parameters are spread across a whole catalogue of automated light-curve fits, and open any one item to inspect its fit and component values.

data.text: Output tables from an automated fitting pipeline. There is one table of whole-object fits and two tables of fitted components (one row per component), plus a pre-rendered figure of each object's fitted light curve per instrument. The results come in dated, versioned releases.
data.item: one transient source with its fitted underlying decay model and its fitted flare or pulse components

stage.text: exploring and checking the output of an automated light-curve fitting pipeline across a catalogue, before population analysis

mechanism.text: A configurable scatter plot of the whole population, with dropdowns for the axes, log/linear switches, colouring by a third parameter and highlighting of named items, is linked to a per-item detail page. Clicking a point switches to that item's page, which shows its fit figures and component tables. The highlighted items and axis choices persist across page changes.

field.text: light-curve model fitting and population parameter statistics in high-energy astrophysics

workflow.name: survey a catalogue of fitted results and open any one item's fit

steps.here: A sidebar dropdown picks a results release, labelled by date and pipeline version, and loads its tables of whole-object fits, flares and pulses.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Population Statistics plots the whole catalogue. The person chooses the population (Afterglows or Pulses/Flares), sets the X and Y parameters, and switches each axis between linear and log scale.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Toggles show flares, pulses or both. 'Color By' adds a third parameter as a colour scale, or 'Specific GRB' highlights named items, which stay highlighted as the axes change.

Hovering a point shows its values. Clicking a point opens that item in the Burst Viewer, or the person types a name into its search box. The page header then lists summary values and component counts.

steps.step: read the fitted model for each instrument
steps.here: Each instrument section shows the fitted light-curve figure. Next to it are the conversion factor, temporal indices, break times and fluences, then a table of each pulse or flare's timing and energetics. An expander shows the model's function parameters.

steps.step: check how each value was defined
steps.here: The About page has tabs describing each instrument's fitting method and a table giving every parameter's unit and formula.

distinctive: Components from two instruments, X-ray flares and gamma-ray pulses, can be plotted on the same axes with different colours and symbols, and either set can be turned off.
Derived energetics (fluence from a count-to-flux conversion, isotropic energy, peak and mean luminosity) sit alongside the raw fit parameters and can be chosen as axes.
Axes default to log scale, and log-valued columns are computed in advance so a colour scale can span orders of magnitude.
Named items stay highlighted while the person changes axes or switches between populations, so they can be followed through many parameter pairs.
Several dated pipeline releases can be selected, so results from different versions of the fitter can be browsed.

parts.title: Results release selector
parts.summary: A sidebar dropdown that picks a dated, versioned release of the pipeline output and loads its three result tables and the list of item names.

parts.title: Population Statistics
parts.summary: A page that switches between the whole-object and the component populations, derives the plottable and log-scaled columns with their units, and passes them to the scatter plot.

parts.title: Axis, scale and colour controls
parts.summary: Dropdowns for the X and Y parameters, linear/log switches, a colour-by choice, a multi-select that highlights named items, and toggles for each component population. The choices persist between visits.

parts.title: Population scatter plot
parts.summary: Plots every item or component by the two chosen parameters, with unit labels and an optional colour scale. Highlighted items are drawn large on top, hovering shows values, and clicking a point opens that item in the Burst Viewer.

parts.title: Burst Viewer
parts.summary: A searchable page for one item. It normalises the typed name, gathers that item's rows from all three tables, and shows a header of summary values such as duration, redshift, fluence and component counts.

parts.title: Gamma-ray instrument fit and pulse table
parts.summary: Shows the fitted gamma-ray light-curve figure beside the count-to-flux conversion, its fit quality and the total pulse fluence. Below is a table of each pulse's timing and energetics, with an expander for the pulse model's parameters.

parts.title: X-ray instrument fit and flare table
parts.summary: Shows the fitted X-ray light-curve figure beside the broken power law's temporal indices and break times (with errors) and the afterglow and total flare fluences. Below is a table of each flare's timing and energetics, with an expander for the flare model's parameters.

parts.title: About LAFF
parts.summary: A tabbed reference page. It gives an overview of the catalogue with live counts, describes each instrument's fitting procedure and the flare/pulse model formula, and has tables of every parameter with its unit and how it was computed.
